papers.title_in_file: Enhancing GPU-acceleration in the Python-based Simulations of Chemistry Framework
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: An industrial team's description of GPU acceleration of classical DFT quantum chemistry in the open-source GPU4PySCF package, with benchmarks against Q-Chem on CPUs.

assertions.value: The authors report that GPU4PySCF delivers 30 times speedup over a 32-core CPU node on modern GPU platforms for DFT calculations, resulting in approximately 90% cost savings for most DFT tasks.
quotes: GPU4PySCF delivers 30 times speedup over a 32-core CPU node, resulting in approximately 90% cost savings for most DFT tasks
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors are the industrial contributors describing their own package (ByteDance Research); benchmark in Section 2.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a classical GPU simulation of quantum chemistry, a baseline for classical simulation cost, not a quantum computation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, on average, GPU4PySCF is 20 times faster than identical SCF calculations in Q-Chem 6.1 on 32 CPU cores, and 50 times faster for Hessian calculations.
quotes: On average, GPU4PySCF achieves a performance that is 20 times faster than identical SCF calculations performed using Q-Chem 6.1 on 32 CPU cores
This speedup increases dramatically to 50 times for Hessian calculations
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2.2 benchmark by the package authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that they benchmark the speedup only across molecules containing 20-84 atoms, and that their implementations are not optimal and have many current limitations.
quotes: We only benchmark the speedup across molecules containing 20-84 atoms.
our implementations are certainly not optimal and there are many current limitations
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own benchmark scope (Section 2.2, p.5) and limits (Section 5, p.25).

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a variational embedding classifier for analog quantum computers such as quantum annealers and tests it by numerical simulation on circles and MNIST digits.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical simulations in which their classifier reaches train and test accuracy above 99.5% on a 2-circle concentric circles dataset, and state that it can reach accuracy comparable with the best classical classifiers.
assertions.anchor: Sections III and IV, pp.7-8; Abstract
quotes: As a comparison, for our classifier, the train and test accuracy are (> 99.5%, > 99.5%) for 2-circle case
Our classifier can reach accuracy comparable with the best classical classifiers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulation on small benchmark datasets (Section IV).
assertions.reader_inference: Simulated results on toy datasets, not hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that the number of optimization parameters of their classifier scales linearly with the number of qubits.
quotes: the number of optimization parameters of our classifier scales linearly with the number of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from the stated construction of the classifier (Section II, parameter count of the linear transformation).

assertions.value: The authors state that they performed numerical simulations, and list experimental realization on actual quantum computers as a topic for future investigation.
quotes: We performed numerical simulations that demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm for performing binary and multi-class classification
the experimental realization on actual quantum computers, etc., can be investigated.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope: simulation only (Abstract) and hardware realization left open (Section V).

assertions.value: The authors report that the performance of their classifier can be increased by increasing the number of qubits until the performance saturates and fluctuates.
quotes: We find that the performance of our classifier can be increased by increasing the number of qubits until the performance saturates and fluctuates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations (Figure 5, Tables).

papers.title_in_file: A generalized cycle benchmarking algorithm for characterizing mid-circuit measurements
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Theory and simulation of a cycle benchmarking type protocol for characterizing noisy mid-circuit measurements, with a learnability theory.

assertions.value: The authors develop a cycle benchmarking type algorithm to characterize noisy mid-circuit measurements, whose key idea is a joint Fourier transform on the classical and quantum registers.
quotes: In this work we develop a cycle benchmarking (CB)-type algorithm to characterize noisy MCMs.
The key idea is to use a joint Fourier transform on the classical and quantum registers
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract and Section I describe the protocol the paper defines.

assertions.value: The paper proves that its protocol is complete: the space of learnable information equals the cycle space, so all learnable information can be learned using the algorithm.
quotes: The protocol in Theorem 1 is complete in the sense that the space of learnable information FL is equal to the cycle space Z.
which shows that all learnable information can be learned using our algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 2, Section V (proof given in the paper).

assertions.value: The authors state that certain parameters are coupled with gauge transformations and cannot be precisely learned SPAM-robustly, and that whether the entire cycle space can be learned through concatenation remains an open question.
quotes: Namely, we show that certain parameters are coupled with gauge transformations, thus cannot be precisely learned SPAM-robustly.
remains an open question.
assertions.certainty_reason: Discussion and outlook, Section VIII, states these limits of the work.

papers.title_in_file: Entanglement-induced provable and robust quantum learning advantages
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Proves a noise-robust constant-versus-linear quantum learning advantage on a designed translation task, with simulations and an IonQ Aria experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state they design a task that quantum models with a constant number of parameters can solve with certainty using entanglement, and that they rigorously prove commonly-used classical ML models must scale at least linearly with the size of the task for accuracy larger than an exponentially small value.
quotes: we design a task that can be solved with certainty by quantum models with a constant number of parameters using entanglement
we rigorously prove that commonly-used classical ML models must scale at least linearly with the size of the task
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (noiseless) with proof in the Supplementary Materials; noisy case in Theorem 2.
assertions.reader_inference: The classical bound holds for communication-bounded models on this specific task.

assertions.value: The authors state that the advantage is only aimed at constant-versus-linear separation over commonly-used classical ML models (autoregressive and encoder-decoder models), that the task is contrivedly designed to exemplify entanglement reducing classical communication, and that stronger advantages against broader families of classical algorithms are left to future work.
quotes: only aiming at constant-versus-linear advantage over commonly-used classical ML models (i.e., autoregressive and encoder-decoder models)

the quantum advantage explored in this paper builds upon a specific family of translation tasks that are contrivedly designed to best exemplify the role of entanglement in reducing classical communication
We leave to future work the problem of finding stronger advantages that are provable against broader families of classical algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limits in Section III.

assertions.value: The authors report experiments on IonQ's 25-qubit trapped-ion device Aria in which the scores achieved are consistently above 0.88 for up to problem size n = 24.
quotes: we carry out experiments on IonQ's 25-qubit trapped-ion quantum device Aria via Amazon Web Services (AWS)
We find that the scores achieved on current quantum devices are consistently above 0.88 for up to problem size n = 24.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single empirical experiment (Figure 2b).

papers.title_in_file: Optimal storage capacity of quantum Hopfield neural networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper extending Gardner's approach to compute the optimal storage capacity of quantum Hopfield-type networks, applied to an open driven-dissipative spin model.

assertions.value: The authors propose a general method for evaluating the maximal storage capacity of quantum neural network models, and exploit the theory of classical spin glasses to derive the optimal storage capacity of quantum networks with quenched pattern variables.
quotes: we propose and explore a general method for evaluating the maximal storage capacity of quantum neural network models.
we exploit the theory of classical spin glasses for deriving the optimal storage capacity of quantum networks with quenched pattern variables
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the method the paper develops.

assertions.value: The authors report that for an open-system quantum associative memory formed of interacting spin-1/2 particles, the maximal storage capacity decreases monotonically upon increasing both temperature and coherent drive, which they say indicates that both quantities introduce noise.
quotes: As an example, we apply our method to an open-system quantum associative memory formed of interacting spin-1/2 particles realizing coupled artificial neurons.
We find that the maximal storage capacity decreases monotonically upon increasing both temperature and coherent drive, which indicates that both quantities introduce noise
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic and numerical result for one model (Results section); the paper presents no hardware test.
assertions.reader_inference: The result concerns one open-system model, so it does not show a quantum storage advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that applications of earlier approaches to specific models do not provide conclusive results with regard to enhanced quantum storage advantage.
quotes: However, applications to specific models do not provide conclusive results with regard to enhanced quantum storage advantage
assertions.certainty_reason: Statement about earlier work, attributed to other papers.

papers.title_in_file: Using a quantum computer to solve a real-world problem - what can be achieved today?
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: An applied study of QAOA, VQE and quantum annealing on an ambulance location problem, mostly on simulators with some QPU and D-Wave runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that their research confirms the broad consensus that quantum gate hardware needs to be much more capable than is available currently in scale and fidelity to address such problems at a commercially valuable level, and that quantum gate computers can currently only complete qualitative demonstrations.
assertions.anchor: Abstract p.1; Section VIII A, p.54
quotes: Our research confirms the broad consensus that quantum gate hardware will need to be much more capable than is available currently in terms of scale and fidelity to be able to address such problems at a commercially valuable level.
Quantum gate computers currently are at the stage where they can only be used to complete qualitative demonstrations of how a problem can be solved.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' conclusion from their experiments on one problem family (Sections VI and VIII).

assertions.value: The authors report that on the D-Wave Advantage annealer they investigated problems up to an 8x8 grid size but found no feasible solutions in their trial runs, and with reverse annealing they were able to solve or get close to the lowest cost solution for problems up to a 6x6 grid with 2 ambulances.
quotes: we were able to investigate problems up to an 8x8 grid size albeit that no feasible solutions were found during our trial runs
we were able to solve or get close to the lowest cost function solution for problems up to a 6x6 grid with 2 ambulances
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results from one study (Section VII).

assertions.value: The authors state that they examined quantum gate based methods mainly using a simulator and quantum annealing using a live system.
quotes: both quantum gate based methods (mainly using a simulator) and quantum annealing (using a live system)
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of their own experimental scope, Section VIII A.

papers.title_in_file: Adversarial Robustness Guarantees for Quantum Classifiers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Theory with numerics proving robustness guarantees for quantum classifiers against classical adversaries in three attack scenarios.

assertions.value: The authors prove that quantum classifiers are protected against weak perturbations of data drawn from the trained distribution and protected against local attacks if they are insufficiently scrambling.
quotes: we prove that quantum classifiers are: (i) protected against weak perturbations of data drawn from the trained distribution
(ii) protected against local attacks if they are insufficiently scrambling
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2, proofs in Section IV (Methods).

assertions.value: The authors state that their guarantees restrict to the case of a classical adversary whose allowable perturbations are constrained by the data encoding strategy employed by the model.
quotes: by restricting to the physically relevant case of a classical adversary whose allowable perturbations are constrained by the data encoding strategy employed by the model
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own threat model in the Introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that for universal adversarial attacks they show only evidence of protection if the classifier is sufficiently chaotic, and that it remains to be seen how the chaos-based guarantees are consistent with trainability of the safeguarded model.
quotes: (iii) show evidence that they are protected against universal adversarial attacks if they are sufficiently chaotic
it remains to be seen to what extent the chaos-based quantum guarantees of adversarial robustness are consistent with the trainability of the safeguarded model in the first place
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract and Discussion state the limit.

papers.title_in_file: Bayesian Learning of Parameterised Quantum Circuits
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Reformulates training of parameterised quantum circuits as Bayesian inference, with a Laplace-prior dimension reduction and a Langevin sampler, tested on Quantinuum H1-2 and in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report experiments on the Quantinuum H1-2 computer showing that circuits resulting from the Laplace-prior dimension reduction are faster to execute and less noisy than circuits trained without it, with the circuit that had 45% of parameterised gates removed significantly cheaper.
quotes: Experiments on the Quantinuum H1-2 computer show that the resulting circuits are faster to execute and less noisy than the circuits trained without the dimension reduction strategy.
Observe that the circuit with 45% of paramterised gates removed is significantly cheaper
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one experiment on authors' employer's hardware (Figure 7).
assertions.reader_inference: The authors work at Quantinuum, the maker of H1-2.

assertions.value: The authors report that numerical simulations on three different problems show their posterior sampling strategy is capable of generating samples from the full posterior and avoiding local optima.
quotes: Numerical simulations on three different problems show that the strategy is capable of generating samples from the full posterior and avoiding local optima.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result on three problems.

assertions.value: The authors state that both inference algorithms bring an additional tuning parameter, and that they have only investigated point estimate and Monte Carlo approximations to the posterior.
quotes: Both of the described inference algorithms bring with them an additional tuning parameter
Additionally, we have only investigated point estimate and Monte Carlo approximations to the posterior.
assertions.certainty_reason: Discussion, Section VI.
